proposals.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthoborate that should be insulating and chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and Li6PS5Cl. Its high Li content and basic oxide character should make it less prone to the oxidative sulfide decomposition seen with Li3PO4, which produced P2O5, SO2 and SCl4 at the contact. Borates are also reported as sulfide-compatible coating materials.
proposals.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with a wide gap but had a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom, driven by sulfide-oxidizing products (P2O5, SO2, SCl4). That penalty is far above the 0.05 eV acceptance threshold, so I want a different, more Li-rich oxyanion chemistry.

proposals.motivation: Both oxyanion coatings failed: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.337, P2O5/SO2/SCl4 products) and Li3BO3 (penalty 0.725, B2O3/BPO4/SCl4 products). Both showed sulfide-oxidizing contact products, so I am switching to the halide family.
